competitors.name: MyFitnessPal
competitors.market_position: Market leader with largest user base
competitors.what_they_do: Traditional calorie tracking with large food database (millions of foods), barcode scanning (premium only since 2022), macro tracking, exercise logging
weaknesses: 2026 redesign added friction (90s → several minutes per log)
97% of users unhappy with premium pricing
Barcode scanning moved to paywall in 2022
Excessive ads even for premium users

user_quotes.quote: The 2026 MyFitnessPal redesign added friction with more taps to log a meal, a diary that no longer shows calories per meal at a glance, and removed or hidden shortcuts like copy-meal and multi-select. Users report their daily logging routine went from 90 seconds to several minutes
Free features have become more restricted, ads more prominent, and feature development has slowed while newer competitors have built AI-native experiences that feel significantly more modern

competitors.recent_activity: Acquired Cal AI (March 2026) and Intent meal planning app (2025), added ChatGPT Health integration (Jan 2026)
competitors.threat_level: MEDIUM (vulnerable to disruption despite market position)

competitors.name: Cronometer
competitors.what_they_do: Deep micronutrient tracking (84 nutrients), most precise database, barcode scanner, therapeutic diet support

user_quotes.quote: For nutrient depth, Cronometer shines. Tracks 84 micronutrients — iron, zinc, vitamin D, B12, and more. Excellent for managing specific health conditions or following therapeutic diets

competitors.threat_level: LOW (different target market: health-focused power users)

competitors.name: Vora
competitors.what_they_do: Faster logging, deep nutrient tracking, nutrition as part of complete health platform, generous free tier
weaknesses: Newer entrant with less brand recognition

user_quotes.quote: Best for people who want faster logging, deep nutrient tracking, and nutrition as part of a complete health platform with a genuinely useful free tier

competitors.threat_level: MEDIUM (directly competing on speed and user experience)

competitors.name: Nutrola
competitors.what_they_do: Snap & Track AI - photo of meal → automatic identification, portion estimation, calorie/macro logging in <3 seconds
strengths: Handles homemade dishes and regional cuisines
weaknesses: AI accuracy issues for complex meals
Limited control when AI makes mistakes

user_quotes.quote: Snap & Track AI: Take a photo of any meal and Nutrola identifies the food, estimates portion sizes, and logs the calories and macros in under three seconds. It handles homemade dishes, restaurant plates, and regional cuisines that other apps struggle with

competitors.threat_level: MEDIUM (competing on speed, but AI accuracy is limiting factor)

competitors.name: SnapCalorie
competitors.what_they_do: AI-powered photo calorie counting with voice, picture, or label input
weaknesses: Unreliable AI - sometimes wrong food type or 2x weight error
Limited ability to correct AI mistakes

user_quotes.quote: The AI function is not reliable - sometimes it's amazingly accurate, but other times it gets the type of food wrong or it will misjudge the weight by a factor of two. For example, in a salad, chopped avocado was counted as chopped cucumber
SnapCalorie is on average around 15% mean caloric error (that's +/- 150 calories on a 1000 calorie dish)

competitors.name: Cal AI
competitors.what_they_do: AI photo recognition for calorie tracking
strengths: Reasonable accuracy for simple Western foods

user_quotes.quote: Cal AI provides reasonable calorie estimates for simple, clearly visible Western foods, but accuracy decreases significantly for complex meals, homemade dishes because it relies on AI estimation without cross-referencing a verified database

competitors.recent_activity: Acquired by MyFitnessPal in early March 2026

competitors.name: Lose It!
competitors.what_they_do: Large food database (10M+ foods), barcode scanning, macro tracking, exercise logging, goal customization
competitors.pricing: Free version includes barcode scanning, premium available
competitors.threat_level: MEDIUM (direct MFP alternative but same manual entry friction)

competitors.name: MacroFactor
competitors.what_they_do: Advanced macro coaching with adaptive algorithms
competitors.threat_level: LOW (different market segment: serious fitness tracking)

competitors.name: Foodnoms
competitors.what_they_do: Simple, customizable, privacy-friendly tracking built for Apple devices
competitors.threat_level: LOW (niche: Apple users who value privacy)

delivery_platform_integration.current_state: NO direct consumer nutrition apps with delivery platform integration found

uber_eats.consumer_api: Merchant-focused APIs only. OAuth 2.0, whitelisting required
uber_eats.nutrition_data: Not explicitly available via public consumer API

doordash.business_api: DoorDash for Business API available for enterprise meal programs

plaid.transaction_data: Can identify DoorDash/UberEats transactions as 'marketplace' type with 90%+ categorization accuracy
plaid.nutrition_data: No - only transaction history, not order details

receipt_ocr.technology: 2026 transformer-based AI models can extract 40+ fields including itemized line items
receipt_ocr.accuracy: High for discrete items (grocery), lower for restaurant aggregated totals
receipt_ocr.nutrition_link: No automatic nutrition linking - would require manual mapping

integration_opportunities: Transaction-based import via Plaid API (can identify delivery orders, but no item-level data)
Receipt OCR parsing (can extract items, but requires nutrition database mapping)
Email receipt parsing (UberEats/DoorDash send detailed email receipts with itemized orders)
Unified food delivery APIs (KitchenHub, MealMe) - focus on restaurant POS, not consumer nutrition
delivery_platform_integration.gap_analysis: MAJOR OPPORTUNITY: No existing consumer app automatically imports delivery orders into calorie tracking. All current solutions require manual re-entry.

market_trends.shift_to_ai: Market moving from manual entry to AI photo tracking, but accuracy remains a blocker
market_trends.premium_fatigue: Users frustrated with expensive subscriptions and features behind paywalls
market_trends.workplace_meals: 24% of Bay Area delivery orders after 6pm are workplace orders, growing trend for late-night office meals
market_trends.api_ecosystem: Nutrition APIs (Nutritionix, Edamam, Spoonacular) mature and available, but not connected to delivery platforms
